position.identity: Benson S. Hsu, MD, MBA. Pediatric intensivist and former health system executive. I build with AI, run the data, and decide what's worth it.
position.promise: I help health systems, investors and companies decide which clinical AI to trust, invest in and build on, and how to get it adopted and grow it safely.
position.proof: Every decision is backed by a lab: builds with current models, dated, with the results reported, including what broke, and a verdict on each.
position.method: Four stages: Strategy, Build or buy, Rules, Proof. Every entry and every memo ends in a verdict: Build, Buy, Skip or Wait.

signature_block.name: Benson S. Hsu, MD, MBA

stages.name: Strategy
stages.question: Is it worth doing, worth investing in, and what will it cost, save or earn?
stages.background: I was a health system vice president and worked on the payer side. Duke MBA. Advisory roles at McKinsey and Bain.

stages.name: Build or buy
stages.question: Build, buy, partner or wait? Is the vendor's claim true? Where is it worth building our own?
stages.background: I built five tools with current models and agents in 2026, and before that ran a health system's data function.

stages.name: Rules
stages.question: How do we approve, govern, and keep it safe as it grows?
stages.background: I have sat on guideline panels, written national society protocols, and worked on health system AI governance.

stages.name: Proof
stages.question: Does it work here, on our patients, and does it still work on this year's models?
stages.background: I ran enterprise data and analytics. In 2026 I checked my own papers against their files and retired two. Verdicts are re-tested quarterly.

pivot_story: I built five clinical AI tools in a year.
I tested whether any had a moat, and none did.
I learned the hard part is deciding what's safe and worth it, and proving it.
This site is how I do that, for my own tools and for yours.

doors.line: One memo on one tool. It says Build, Buy, Skip or Wait, and lists what your governance committee will need to see.
A diligence read in five to ten business days. It says whether the clinical AI is real and safe, and what you could not defend later.
The clinical half of your engagement, by the day or by the project, run on the four-stage method.

lines.lab_scope: The lab's evidence to date is pediatric. The method is not.
lines.candidate_not_clinical: The pathways are candidates for a physician to review. None is for clinical use.
lines.verdict_definition: The verdict tells a buyer what to do, Build, Buy, Skip or Wait. It does not grade the work.

how_entries_written: Four sections in one order: worth doing, build or buy, rules, is it working.
The identity line first; the verdict last, with one line of reasoning and one line on what it is worth to a buyer.
Dated. Numbers only from a public deposit or a named source; retired figures never reappear.
Model names reported neutrally. Pathways are candidates, not clinical documents.

disclosure: Tools were built on my own time with no institutional data. Advisory work is disclosed to my employer.

offers_summary: Three reads, in 5, 10 or 15 business days, and a day rate for consulting partners. One fixed fee, in writing, before I start.
how_i_write: Every entry runs in the same order: is it worth doing, build or buy, what rules apply, is it working. It opens with who I am and closes with a verdict, one line on why, and one line on what it is worth to you. Every number comes from a public deposit or a named source, and a figure I have retired does not come back in another form. I name the models I used and report them without favor. Where a paper is under review I say so, and its numbers may move. From 2027, one entry a quarter.
